source.board: National Council of Examiners for Engineering and Surveying (NCEES)
source.qualification: NCEES FE Chemical CBT Exam Specifications

chemical-engineering.note: Units follow the NCEES FE Chemical specification's knowledge areas in exam order, from mathematics through transport phenomena to process design and safety.

units.title: Material and energy balances
topics: Reactive systems and extent of reaction

lesson.title: Material and Energy Balances
lesson.summary: The accountant's toolkit of chemical engineering — balancing mass and energy around any process.

lesson.title: Fluid Flow in Process Piping
lesson.summary: Moving fluids at scale — pipe-flow equations, friction losses and how pumps are chosen.

lesson.title: Heat Transfer and Heat Exchangers
lesson.summary: Moving heat on purpose — resistances in series, LMTD design and the geometry of exchangers.

lesson.title: Separations: Distillation and Beyond
lesson.summary: The heart of process engineering — distillation stages, absorption columns and membrane separations.

lesson.title: Reaction Engineering and Reactor Design
lesson.summary: Designing reactors — rate laws, ideal reactor models and the trade-offs between them.

lesson.title: Process Thermodynamics
lesson.summary: The thermodynamic backbone — equations of state, phase equilibrium and the cycles that power plants.

lesson.title: Process Design and Economics
lesson.summary: From concept to PFD — flowsheet logic and the cost estimates that decide projects.

lesson.title: Process Safety and Control
lesson.summary: Designing against failure — HAZOP, relief systems and the control loops that keep plants stable.

source.board: National Council of Examiners for Engineering and Surveying (NCEES)
source.qualification: NCEES FE Civil CBT Exam Specifications

civil-engineering.note: Units follow the NCEES FE Civil specification's knowledge areas in exam order — mechanics and materials first, then the five civil disciplines from water to construction.

units.title: Statics and dynamics for civil systems

lesson.title: Statics and Dynamics for Civil Engineers
lesson.summary: The mechanics every civil engineer uses — trusses, internal forces and moving loads.

lesson.title: Mechanics of Materials
lesson.summary: How structures carry load — stress states, beam bending and the buckling of slender columns.

lesson.title: Structural Analysis and Design
lesson.summary: From analysis to code-compliant design — how beams and frames are checked and sized.

lesson.title: Geotechnical Engineering
lesson.summary: Building on dirt safely — soil mechanics, effective stress and foundation design.

lesson.title: Hydraulics and Water Systems
lesson.summary: Water infrastructure mechanics — hydrostatics, pipe systems and channels.

lesson.title: Hydrology and Flood Analysis
lesson.summary: Where the water goes — rainfall-runoff, design storms and flood-frequency statistics.

lesson.title: Transportation Engineering
lesson.summary: Moving people safely — road geometry, pavement layers and traffic-flow theory.

lesson.title: Environmental Engineering
lesson.summary: Protecting health at scale — treatment trains, air quality and waste systems.

lesson.title: Construction and Engineering Economics
lesson.summary: Getting it built — schedules, estimates and the time-value mathematics of projects.

source.board: National Council of Examiners for Engineering and Surveying (NCEES)
source.qualification: NCEES FE Mechanical CBT Exam Specifications

mechanical-engineering.note: Units follow the NCEES FE Mechanical specification's knowledge areas in exam order, from mathematics and statics through design, thermal-fluids and HVAC.

units.title: Mathematics, statics and dynamics
topics: Kinematics and kinetics of rigid bodies

lesson.title: Mechanics Foundations
lesson.summary: The mechanical engineer's bedrock — vectors, rigid-body motion and the conservation laws.

units.title: Mechanics of materials and machine design

lesson.title: Machine Design and Failure
lesson.summary: Designing parts that survive — stress states, fatigue and the standard machine elements.

lesson.title: Engineering Thermodynamics
lesson.summary: Energy accounting for machines — the laws, entropy and the cycles behind engines and chillers.

lesson.title: Fluid Mechanics for Machines
lesson.summary: Fluids in machines — pipe losses, lift and drag, and how pumps and turbines work.

lesson.title: Heat Transfer in Engineering
lesson.summary: Thermal design — conduction paths, convective coefficients and radiator/exchanger sizing.

lesson.title: HVAC and Psychrometrics
lesson.summary: Conditioning air — the psychrometric chart, load calculations and refrigeration plant.

lesson.title: Measurement and Control
lesson.summary: Knowing and controlling the machine — sensors, error, and first feedback loops.

lesson.title: Manufacturing Processes
lesson.summary: How parts are made — casting, forming, machining and the rise of additive manufacturing.

source.board: National Council of Examiners for Engineering and Surveying (NCEES)
source.qualification: NCEES FE Electrical and Computer CBT Exam Specifications
source.track: professional licensure · Fundamentals of Engineering (Electrical & Computer)

electrical-engineering.note: Units follow the NCEES FE Electrical and Computer specification's knowledge areas, from circuit analysis through electronics, power, signals and control.

lesson.title: DC Circuit Analysis
lesson.summary: The grammar of circuits — Kirchhoff's laws, node analysis and equivalent sources.

units.title: Circuit analysis II: AC and transients

lesson.title: AC Circuits and Transients
lesson.summary: Alternating current as algebra — phasors, impedance and the behaviour of RLC networks.

lesson.title: Electronic Devices and Amplifiers
lesson.summary: Semi-conducting workhorses — diodes, transistors and the op-amp's near-ideal magic.

lesson.title: Digital Logic and Microcontrollers
lesson.summary: Computing in hardware — gates, flip-flops, state machines and the embedded microcontroller.

lesson.title: Electromagnetics and Transmission Lines
lesson.summary: Fields that carry power and signals — Maxwell's equations and the lossy realities of lines.

lesson.title: Power Systems and Electric Machines
lesson.summary: The grid's machinery — three-phase power, transformers and rotating machines.

lesson.title: Signals and Transforms
lesson.summary: Signals as sums of sinusoids — Fourier analysis, Laplace tools and the sampling theorem.

lesson.title: Control and Communications
lesson.summary: Closing loops and sending messages — stability, modulation schemes and system budgets.

source.qualification: ABET Program Criteria — Aerospace and Similarly Named Engineering Programs

aerospace-engineering.note: Units follow ABET's required aerospace curriculum areas — aerodynamics, structures, propulsion and flight mechanics, with orbital mechanics and systems design.

lesson.title: Aerodynamics I: Lift and Airfoils
lesson.summary: Why wings generate lift — flow over airfoils, pressure distributions and the lift equation.

lesson.title: Compressible Flow and Supersonics
lesson.summary: Past the sound barrier — compressibility, shocks and the regimes of high-speed flight.

lesson.title: Flight Structures and Materials
lesson.summary: Building light and strong — load paths, semi-monocoque construction and composite fatigue.

lesson.title: Flight Mechanics and Performance
lesson.summary: How aircraft fly well — performance envelopes, stability and the equations of motion.

lesson.title: Propulsion: Engines and Rockets
lesson.summary: Making thrust — gas-turbine cycles, afterburners and the rocket equation's tyranny.

lesson.title: Orbital Mechanics
lesson.summary: The mathematics of orbit — Kepler's laws in engineering terms, transfers and pointing.

lesson.title: Flight Control and Avionics
lesson.summary: From cables to software — fly-by-wire, autopilots and the sensor suite.

units.title: Aircraft and spacecraft design
topics: The design loop and trade studies

lesson.title: Aerospace Systems Design
lesson.summary: Putting it together — the design spiral, certification and how missions get specified.

source.qualification: ABET Program Criteria — Biomedical and Similarly Named Engineering Programs

biomedical-engineering.note: Units follow ABET's required biomedical curriculum areas — physiology for engineers, biomaterials, biomechanics, bioinstrumentation and the regulatory path.

lesson.title: Physiology for Engineers
lesson.summary: The body as a system of pumps, filters and signals — the physiology every BME needs.

lesson.title: Biomaterials and Implants
lesson.summary: Materials the body accepts — biocompatibility, degradation and implant design.

lesson.title: Biomechanics
lesson.summary: Mechanics of living tissue — bones, ligaments, prosthetics and gait analysis.

lesson.title: Bioinstrumentation and Biosignals
lesson.summary: Reading the body electric — electrodes, biopotential amplifiers and imaging physics.

lesson.title: Tissue Engineering
lesson.summary: Growing replacement tissue — scaffolds, signalling and the challenge of vascularisation.

lesson.title: Medical Device Design
lesson.summary: Designing for the clinic — design controls, sterilisation and human-factors engineering.

lesson.title: Regulatory Pathways and Quality Systems
lesson.summary: Getting devices to patients legally — 510(k), PMA and the quality systems behind them.

units.title: Frontiers: AI, wearables and precision medicine

lesson.title: Frontiers in Biomedical Engineering
lesson.summary: Where the field is heading — wearables, diagnostic AI and engineered therapies.

source.qualification: SWEBOK Guide V4.0 — Software Engineering Body of Knowledge

software-engineering.note: Units follow the SWEBOK Guide V4.0 knowledge areas in order — requirements through construction, testing, maintenance, and the management and professional practices around them.

lesson.title: Software Requirements
lesson.summary: Deciding what to build — elicitation, user stories, and the non-functional requirements that sink projects.

lesson.title: Software Design and Architecture
lesson.summary: Structuring systems for change — cohesion, coupling, patterns and architectural styles.

lesson.title: Construction: Code, APIs and Review
lesson.summary: Writing code that teams can live with — style, API design, git workflows and review culture.

lesson.title: Testing and Quality Assurance
lesson.summary: Proving it works — unit to end-to-end testing, coverage metrics and static analysis.

lesson.title: Maintenance, Debt and Refactoring
lesson.summary: Software is never finished — technical debt, refactoring strategies and evolving legacy systems.

lesson.title: DevOps and Continuous Delivery
lesson.summary: Shipping continuously — pipelines, infrastructure as code and production observability.

lesson.title: Process and Project Management
lesson.summary: Organising the work — agile ceremonies, estimation and managing delivery risk.

lesson.title: Security and Professional Practice
lesson.summary: Engineering responsibly — threat modelling, secure SDLC and the profession's ethics.

source.board: NIST (US National Institute of Standards and Technology)
source.qualification: NICE Workforce Framework for Cybersecurity (NIST SP 800-181r1)
source.track: national framework · workforce categories and competencies

cybersecurity.note: Units follow the NICE Framework's category structure — securely provision, operate and defend, oversee and govern, protect and defend, analyse, and collect and operate.

lesson.title: Security Foundations: the CIA Triad
lesson.summary: The shared language of security — confidentiality, integrity, availability and risk.

lesson.title: Networking and OS for Defenders
lesson.summary: You can't defend what you don't understand — the network and OS mechanics attacks exploit.

lesson.title: Applied Cryptography
lesson.summary: Mathematics as armour — ciphers, hashes, PKI and what TLS actually does.

lesson.title: How Attacks Work
lesson.summary: Thinking like the adversary — kill chains, common exploits and the psychology of phishing.

lesson.title: Defensive Operations and Incident Response
lesson.summary: Blue-team craft — layered defence, detection pipelines and the IR lifecycle.

lesson.title: Governance, Risk and Compliance
lesson.summary: Security as management — policy hierarchies, risk registers and compliance regimes.

lesson.title: Cloud and Application Security
lesson.summary: Securing the modern stack — cloud responsibilities, OWASP risks and supply chains.

lesson.title: Zero Trust and Emerging Threatscapes
lesson.summary: Where security is heading — zero-trust architecture, operational technology and AI on both sides.

source.qualification: Modern Robotics: Mechanics, Planning, and Control
source.document: Canonical open textbook, chapter structure (official companion site)

robotics.note: Units follow the textbook's chapter arc — configuration space, rigid-body kinematics, then forward/inverse kinematics, dynamics, trajectory generation and motion planning.

units.title: Configuration space
topics: Degrees of freedom and Grubler's formula

lesson.title: Configuration Space
lesson.summary: The robot state as a point in space — DOF counting and the geometry of what a robot can be.

lesson.title: Rigid-Body Motions
lesson.summary: Representing motion — rotations, transforms and the exponential map that unifies them.

lesson.title: Forward and Inverse Kinematics
lesson.summary: From joints to gripper and back — product-of-exponentials, IK and Jacobians.

lesson.title: Robot Dynamics
lesson.summary: Forces behind motion — Lagrangian dynamics, inertial coupling and dynamic manipulability.

lesson.title: Motion Planning
lesson.summary: Getting from A to B without collisions — interpolators, RRT and probabilistic roadmaps.

lesson.title: Robot Control
lesson.summary: Making arms precise — joint control, computed torque and interacting with the world safely.

lesson.title: Perception, Estimation and SLAM
lesson.summary: Knowing where you are — sensor fusion, Kalman filters and simultaneous localisation and mapping.

lesson.title: Mobile Robots and Learning Frontiers
lesson.summary: Robots in the wild — navigation stacks, legged locomotion and the learning revolution.

source.qualification: IGDA Curriculum Framework: The Study of Games and Game Development

game-development.note: Units follow the IGDA framework's knowledge areas — game design, programming, art and production — closing with the business and culture of the industry.

lesson.title: Game Design Foundations
lesson.summary: The atoms of play — the MDA framework, core loops and paper prototyping.

lesson.title: Engines and the Game Loop
lesson.summary: Under the hood — the update-render loop, ECS architecture and real-time collision.

lesson.title: Game Graphics and Rendering
lesson.summary: Pixels at 60fps — geometry pipelines, shaders and keeping the frame budget.

lesson.title: Mathematics for Games
lesson.summary: The maths behind the magic — transforms, quaternions and the curves of motion.

lesson.title: Level and Narrative Design
lesson.summary: Space and story — pacing through levels and the machinery of interactive narrative.

lesson.title: Game AI and Procedural Generation
lesson.summary: Faking intelligence well — behaviour trees, pathfinding and worlds that build themselves.

lesson.title: Audio, Feel and Accessibility
lesson.summary: What makes games feel good — sound design, game feel and designing for every player.

lesson.title: Game Production and Business
lesson.summary: Games as products — production pipelines, business models and going to market.
